Fresh floods and landslides set off by heavy rain and storms have killed at least 14 people in Nepal and left another 11 missing, with authorities warning on Sunday that more flash floods were possible. The warnings covered 49 of Nepal's 77 districts, more than half of which faced a high risk of flooding, as water levels in major rivers kept rising. The video filmed at 5:30pm, local time, on Sunday, September 27 shows the latest destruction. It comes after a glacier collapsed near the border with China's Tibet Autonomous Region in late August, sending landslides and a flash flood through valleys downstream and killing more than 1,450 people. #ABCNews #Nepal #Landslide #Floods

Why Is Nepal’s Young Generation Leaving the Country? It’s not just about earning more money abroad — it’s about wanting a better quality of life. In Nepal, even basic tasks like getting a passport, renewing a license, or dealing with government offices can become stressful and time-consuming. Poor roads, complicated procedures, and inefficient public services add to the frustration. Meanwhile, many young people look abroad for systems that work, services they can rely on, and a life with less unnecessary stress. The private sector can create jobs and drive innovation, but public services like roads, passports, and licenses are responsibilities the government must deliver effectively. 🔥 If Nepal wants its youth to stay, it must offer more than opportunities — it must build a system where living and working here feels worthwhile. The question isn’t just why our youth are leaving. It’s what we’re doing to give them a reason to stay. #Nepal #BrainDrain #YouthMigration #NepalEconomy #GovernmentReform #PublicServices #NepaliYouth #DigitalNepal #NepalBusiness #DreamBusiness
